description:
Mission Statement

Driven by the same relentless spirit of scientific inquiry and ingenuity found in Andy Weir's Project Hail Mary, Project Hail Mars is a team dedicated to chronicling humanity's journey across the cosmos. We bring space science to life for the next generation of explorers, engineers, and dreamers by turning real NASA history into compelling, immersive storytelling.
summary: Beetle: The Last Civilization is an interactive story and game that brings NASA's Mars exploration to life. Seventeen years after a dust storm silenced the Beetle rover, a faint signal reaches Earth. NASA sends ARES, an AI rescue rover, to bring Beetle home. Beneath the surface, they awaken Echo, an ancient machine that remembers a lost Martian civilization. As the three robots travel together, ARES learns to look beyond its programming and finally chooses to save Echo at the cost of itself. Scans then reveal hundreds more buried structures, so the discovery is only the beginning. Our team built the story, the game, a playable website reached by QR code, and 3D-printed models of Beetle, ARES and Echo. The story draws on NASA's Opportunity and Perseverance rovers and Mars orbiter radar, and it makes space science accessible and inspiring while asking whether AI can learn empathy
details: Beetle: The Last Civilization is an interactive story and game inspired by NASA's Mars missions. A QR code opens a website that tells the story in depth: Beetle, a rover lost in a dust storm; ARES, the rescue rover sent to find it; and Echo, an ancient machine that reveals a buried civilization. At the end of the website, visitors play a game based on the story. The story draws on real NASA work: the Opportunity rover's loss in a 2018 global dust storm, the Perseverance rover as the model for ARES, and Mars orbiter radar, which detects hidden features below the surface and inspired how our robots detect the signal and the buried structure where Echo is found. Our intended impact is to make Mars exploration approachable and exciting for students, families and space fans, to spark curiosity that can lead toward science and engineering, and to start a conversation about how humans and AI should work together, shown when ARES chooses to save Echo beyond its programming. We built the website and game by Claude, and Netlify transformed the codes given by Claude to a real thing, and the presentation was built with Claude too. We 3D-printed physical models of Beetle, ARES and Echo using [printer and software]. The project is creative because it combines storytelling, a playable game and handheld physical models, and gives rovers emotional characters. We considered scientific accuracy, accessibility through a simple QR code and web access, readable design, and clear credit for every source and image.
dataRefs: MARS exploration rovers: spirit and opportunity
